title: Rust Workspace, Repository Model, Schema and Validator Conformance

preflight.note: Created and activated after WI052 architecture discovery and before the Rust workspace, repository model, validator implementation, or conformance integration begins.

acceptance_criteria.text: Create a top-level Rust workspace owned by the tooling scope with separate reusable crates for domain types, canonical schema handling, repository discovery/modeling, validation, and a core facade plus a minimal non-Tauri CLI entrypoint; no Tauri dependency is permitted in the reusable domain crates.

Implement typed Rust representations sufficient for validator/repository parity, including lifecycle/status, provenance, work items, acceptance criteria, dependencies, scopes/record identity, evidence references needed by validation, repository identity, and structured diagnostics without replacing the canonical language-neutral on-disk contracts.

Rust schema validation consumes the canonical RepoPact JSON schemas or a mechanically derived packaged representation; there is no second hand-maintained Rust-only schema authority, and schema-library errors are normalized behind RepoPact-owned diagnostic identity/context.

Implement deterministic repository discovery semantics matching the Python reference for governed work items, evidence, applicable contracts, ignored directories, normalized paths, and lifecycle-directory interpretation.

Implement structural Git linked-worktree recognition and repository/common-dir behavior required by current RepoPact semantics; linked worktrees must not be rediscovered as nested governed repository content merely because of filesystem layout.
Preserve the established record-relative source/reference resolution semantics in Rust and add focused parity coverage so Rust does not reinterpret those references as repository-root relative.

Define structured Rust diagnostics with stable code/severity/message and record/path context plus optional field, related-record, and suggested-action data; existing conformance message substrings remain available for legacy compatibility without becoming the only native diagnostic identity.

Implement the semantic validator rules necessary for the published legacy conformance corpus, preserving reference accept/reject behavior for lifecycle/dependency, provenance/completion, schema, status-directory, contract, version/release, active-scope, evidence-linkage, and related governed repository checks represented by the corpus.

Implement the canonical dashboard projection/comparison required to reproduce missing/stale-dashboard validation semantics without granting general mutation authority or silently hand-maintaining the derived dashboard.

Provide a minimal Rust validation executable accepting a repository root and returning zero for accepted repositories and non-zero for rejected or explicitly unsupported repositories, with deterministic diagnostics and no repository mutation during validation.

Run the published Python `repopact.run_conformance --command` alternate-implementation path against the Rust validation executable and pass every legacy validator case; Rust-only unit tests are not a substitute for this gate.
Unsupported Rust semantics fail explicitly and do not mutate state; WI053 does not describe Rust as canonical and does not create a fallback that guesses at unimplemented governance rules.

Keep existing Python validation and WI050 admission/enforcement behavior green and unchanged except for independently proven defects; do not port the WI050 admission, guard, IPC, platform backend, protected service, or enforcement substrate in this work item.
Add executable Windows/Linux/macOS-portable path and repository-topology tests without modifying frozen CI workflows unless separate operator approval is recorded under the frozen-surface contract.

Closeout evidence records the exact Rust surface implemented, Python baseline results, Rust test results, legacy conformance results, linked-worktree/reference parity results, known unsupported/non-parity surfaces, and confirmation that mutation/Tauri/Python-cutover/WI050 migration remain outside WI053.
